cna.headline: Vietnamese coffee farmers ride China's durian wave
cna.teaser: Vietnam only officially entered the Chinese durian market after a 2022 trade protocol but last year became the country's biggest supplier by volume.
fullText: DAK LAK, Vietnam: Vietnam's Central Highlands produces around one-sixth of the world's coffee, but farmers are switching their traditional crop for durian to cash in on surging Chinese demand for the pungent "king of fruits".
"You can live okay with coffee, but it's durian that makes you rich," said Pham Xuan Lan, as he showed AFP journalists around his farm.
Blessed with a tropical climate and rich basalt soil, the lush Central Highlands produces vast quantities of robusta beans, and Vietnam trails only Brazil in coffee output.
But the area dedicated to durian has soared more than fivefold to 200,000ha nationwide over the past decade, according to the agriculture ministry.
Lan was an early adopter, diversifying his crop two decades ago and now boasting 400 durian trees in Ea Knuec commune, part of Dak Lak province.
They produce 60 tonnes of the sweet yet smelly fruit, which is driven in frozen containers thousands of kilometres north into China.
The 56-year-old expects to make US$76,000 this year - against US$10,000 had he stayed with just coffee.
"With durian, I bought a car, houses for my children and built a villa for my family," he said, his affluence evident around him.
Other local farmers have followed suit, focusing on the premium Ri6, Musang King and Dona varieties.

During the August-October harvest, Dak Lak's roads are packed with trucks loaded with the spiky fruit, and at a durian festival this month, 525 vehicles formed what the Guinness World Records declared the largest ever parade of fruit-carrying vehicles.
The boom is driven by demand from China, fuelled by a combination of expanding supply and growing popularity on social media, particularly among young people.
On Douyin, China's equivalent of TikTok, videos of users cracking open fruit with their bare hands have been watched billions of times.
"This tastes really sweet. It's almost like it's been coated in sugar," said Douyin influencer Liulianzi in a clip liked more than 17,000 times.
Once a luxury food, increased competition between Thailand and Vietnam and improved transport links have helped cut prices and make the fruit more affordable.
At a durian tasting event in Beijing last month, Ada Song told AFP that she had spent almost 1,000 yuan (US$150) on the fruit in recent weeks.
"I have tried nearly 20 different varieties," Song said.
Durian "tastes just as sweet as cake, without the greasiness and heaviness".
China imported almost US$7.5 billion worth of fresh durian last year, a near 12-fold rise from 2015.
Now Beijing is seeking to boost its homegrown produce, with more than 3,000 hectares of plantations on the southern island province of Hainan, which has a similar climate to northern Vietnam.
But "our Hainan durians will always be just a supplement to Southeast Asian durians", acknowledged Feng Xuejie, a durian expert at the Hainan Academy of Agricultural Sciences.
Vietnam's durian exports are expected to reach US$4 billion this year, up from US$180 million in 2021 - 90 per cent of them going to its northern neighbour.
But in the Central Highlands there are concerns about the reliance on China, as well as the risks of oversupply as more farmers join the rush.
Many anxiously eyed a recent price crash in Malaysia , blamed on an unusually bumper harvest.

Durian growers across Southeast Asia are facing a common enemy — climate change. In Malaysia, soaring temperatures mean more watering, more fertiliser and more pruning, all while fuel and fertiliser costs have climbed due to the war in Iran. Some farmers are turning to technology to adapt, such as installing sensors to monitor rainfall, humidity, soil conditions and temperature.
Many farmers there have also switched to durian, focusing on premium varieties and fresh fruit, although the country has only a small slice of the Chinese market.
Vietnam's government warned in early August of the "risks of oversupply and loss of quality control as the planted area is increasing rapidly".
Farmers warn durian is not a one-way bet, requiring a strict mix of humidity, water and fertilisers.
Lan likened growing it to "raising a child - I can give you all the tricks but I cannot guarantee you similar success".
He still grows coffee as his land is leased from a coffee company, allowing him to hedge his bets.
For some, the durian dream has already turned sour.

economistArticle.title: The Price of Closed Borders: The Economic Toll of Immigration Crackdowns
paras: For decades, the lifeblood of advanced economies has been the steady flow of foreign labor. Whether filling high-tech engineering roles in Silicon Valley or undertaking strenuous construction work in rapidly developing cities, migrant workers plug crucial demographic gaps. However, a growing political appetite for isolationism has thrust immigration crackdowns to the forefront of national agendas, most notably in the United States. While such policies may appease certain domestic voting blocs, they carry a steep and inescapable economic toll.

The most immediate casualty of a sweeping immigration crackdown is the sheer size of the workforce. Countries facing aging populations and plummeting birth rates rely heavily on newcomers to sustain economic momentum. Forcing millions of undocumented workers out or severely curtailing legal visas triggers an immediate labor crunch. Industries like agriculture, hospitality, and construction, which rely on low-wage manual labor, find themselves suddenly hollowed out. Crops rot in fields, and building timelines stretch indefinitely.

Advocates of restrictive immigration argue that shrinking the labor supply will naturally force wages up for native-born workers. While this sounds appealing in theory, the macroeconomic reality is far more sobering. Faced with severe labor shortages, businesses do not just raise wages indefinitely; they are often forced to scale back operations or pass the ballooning costs onto consumers. This fuels persistent inflation, eroding the purchasing power of the very citizens the policies were intended to protect. Moreover, some businesses simply close down or relocate overseas.

Beyond the immediate shock to low-wage industries, a clampdown on highly skilled immigration stifles innovation. Tech hubs and research institutions thrive on global talent. When visa pathways are choked, top-tier engineers, scientists, and entrepreneurs choose other destinations, such as Canada, Singapore, or the European Union. The loss of human capital directly degrades a country's long-term productivity growth. A nation that locks its doors eventually finds itself locked out of the global race for intellectual leadership.

Ultimately, economic growth is a function of labor force growth and productivity. Restricting immigration damages both variables simultaneously. As the workforce contracts and innovation stalls, the broader economy faces a protracted period of stagnation. Policymakers must eventually reckon with the stark trade-off: pursuing short-term populist victories today comes at the expense of prosperity tomorrow.
economistArticle.cn:
几十年来，发达经济体的生命线一直是外国劳工的稳定流入。无论是在硅谷担任高科技工程职位，还是在快速发展的城市中从事艰苦的建筑工作，移民工人填补了关键的人口缺口。然而，对孤立主义日益增长的政治胃口已将打击移民推向了国家议程的前沿，在美利坚合众国尤为显著。虽然这些政策可能会迎合某些国内选民，但它们带来了沉重且不可避免的经济代价。

席卷而来的移民打击行动最直接的受害者是劳动力的规模。面对人口老龄化和生育率骤降的国家，在很大程度上依赖新移民来维持经济增长势头。强迫数百万无证工人离开或严厉限制合法签证会立即引发劳动力危机。依赖低薪手工劳动的农业、酒店业和建筑业等行业会突然发现自己空心化。农作物在田里腐烂，建筑工期无限期延长。

限制移民的倡导者认为，缩小劳动力供应自然会迫使本地工人的工资上涨。虽然这在理论上听起来很有吸引力，但宏观经济现实要冷酷得多。面对严重的劳动力短缺，企业不仅无法无限期地提高工资，反而往往被迫缩减运营规模或将激增的成本转嫁给消费者。这加剧了持续的通货膨胀，侵蚀了这些政策本意要保护的公民的购买力。此外，一些企业干脆倒闭或迁往海外。

除了对低薪行业的直接冲击之外，对高技能移民的限制也扼杀了创新。科技中心和研究机构依靠全球人才而蓬勃发展。当签证渠道被堵塞时，顶尖的工程师、科学家和企业家会选择其他目的地，如加拿大、新加坡或欧盟。人力资本的流失直接降低了一个国家的长期生产力增长。一个锁上大门的国家最终会发现自己被排除在争夺知识领袖地位的全球竞争之外。

归根结底，经济增长是劳动力增长和生产力的函数。限制移民同时损害了这两个变量。随着劳动力收缩和创新停滞，更广泛的经济将面临长期的停滞。政策制定者最终必须在残酷的权衡中做出选择：追求眼前的民粹主义胜利，代价是牺牲未来的繁荣。

gems.s: While such policies may appease certain domestic voting blocs, they carry a steep and inescapable economic toll.
gems.why: This sentence makes excellent use of contrast via 'While' to balance political motivation against harsh economic reality. It uses strong, evocative adjectives like 'steep' and 'inescapable' to make the conclusion feel absolute. 句子巧妙运用‘While’引导让步状语从句，将政治动机与严酷的经济现实进行对比。通过使用‘steep’（沉重的）和‘inescapable’（不可避免的）等极具感染力的形容词，使结论显得不容置疑。

gems.s: A nation that locks its doors eventually finds itself locked out of the global race for intellectual leadership.
gems.why: This sentence employs a powerful rhetorical wordplay with 'locks its doors' versus 'locked out of'. It creates a poetic symmetry that highlights the self-defeating nature of isolationist policies. 句子在‘locks its doors’（锁上大门）与‘locked out of’（被拒之门外）之间运用了精妙的反差与双关。这种极具对称美感的修辞手法，深刻揭示了孤立主义政策自食其果的本质。
